claim: A Nature study reported clonally expanded B cells in MS that bind EBV EBNA1 and GlialCAM, supporting EBV-linked B-cell molecular mimicry context in MS.
future_grounding_route: Use only as segregated EBV-MS mechanistic context unless the project's held immune data are used to test EBNA1/GlialCAM-linked B-cell or APC module predictions with predefined specificity controls.

project_finding_reference.finding_id: EBV/IFN APC imprint downgraded by specificity control

project_use: Sharper EBV-MS external context for V50 review of the EBV/IFN APC imprint downgrade; not evidence that the project's IFN/APC imprint is MS-specific.
relationship_note: The source supports EBV-linked B-cell mechanistic plausibility in MS, but does not directly test the project's APC/IFN imprint specificity controls.

source.citation: Lanz et al. Clonally expanded B cells in multiple sclerosis bind EBV EBNA1 and GlialCAM. Nature. 2022.
source.label: Nature EBNA1/GlialCAM cross-reactive B-cell study

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: PubMed bibliographic metadata and short paraphrase only
source_terms.reuse_notes: V50 stores bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrased claim only; do not redistribute article text or treat it as project-grounded evidence.

why_unverifiable: The project has not rerun the external B-cell antigen-binding experiments or linked them to project module specificity controls.
